discovery: Precision mapping of the cosmic microwave background anisotropies by WMAP, establishing the standard ΛCDM cosmological model

nominees.name: David N. Spergel
nominees.affiliation: Simons Foundation and Princeton University, USA

motivation: The Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe turned cosmology into a precision science. Bennett conceived and led the mission, Page led the design and calibration of its differential radiometers, and Spergel led the statistical analysis that turned full-sky temperature and polarization maps into cosmological parameters with percent-level accuracy. WMAP determined the age, geometry and composition of the Universe: a spatially flat cosmos dominated by dark energy and cold dark matter, with nearly scale-invariant, adiabatic, Gaussian primordial fluctuations and an early reionization epoch. These results independently confirmed the accelerating expansion inferred from supernovae and provided the first strong observational support for the inflationary paradigm's predictions. Its careful control of systematics and open public release of data and likelihood codes set the standard for Planck and for all later large-scale-structure surveys. Today's tests of ΛCDM, including the Hubble tension, are measured against the benchmark WMAP established.
